Surah al-Saffat (The Ranks) [Meccan, and its verses were revealed after al-An'am]

﴿By those who range in ranks, ranging﴾ — the angels, who align themselves in worship, or who spread their wings in the air, awaiting what they are commanded.
﴿By those who drive [the clouds] with a driving⁠—﴾ The angels drive the clouds, that is, they herd them along.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 37, verse 3:

﴿Fa-t-tāliyāt﴾ (By those who recite): i.e., the reciters of the Qur'an, who recite it, ﴿dhikran﴾ (as a remembrance): a verbal noun (maṣdar) derived from the meaning of "al-tāliyāt."
Indeed, your God (﴿Inna ilahakum﴾) — O people of Makkah.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 37, verse 5:

﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts﴾ — i.e., and the wests (al-maghárib), for the sun: for it there is every day a rising-place (mashriq) and a setting-place (maghrib).

﴿Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with adornment: the stars﴾. That is, with its light, or "with it" (the adornment being the stars themselves). The idafa (construction of the noun with its genitive, here *zinat al-kawakib*) is for explanation (*bayan*), as in the reading with tanwin, *bi-zinatin*, where *al-kawakib* (the stars) is what clarifies *zinatin* (adornment).

Wa-ḥifẓan (﴿وحِفْظًا﴾) is in the accusative, governed by a verb that is implied: i.e., "We guarded it with the shooting stars (shuhub)" ﴿from every﴾ (min kulli), which is related to the implied verb, ﴿rebellious devil﴾ (shayṭān mārid), i.e., one who is insolent and has stepped outside obedience.

﴿They cannot listen﴾ — i.e., the devils. This is a new sentence (mustaʾnaf), and their listening is in the sense of what is preserved from it (wa-samāʿuhum huwa fī al-maʿnā al-maḥfūẓ ʿanhu). ﴿to the exalted assembly﴾ — the angels in the heaven. The verb "listen" (samāʿ) is construed with "to" (ilā) because it includes the meaning of "giving ear" (al-iṣghāʾ). In another reading, it is pronounced with a doubled mīm and sīn, its original form being yatasammaʿūna, the tāʾ being assimilated into the sīn. ﴿And they are pelted﴾ — i.e., the devils are pelted with meteors (bi-al-shuhub) ﴿from every side﴾ — from the horizons of the heaven.

﴿Driven away﴾ is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of دَحَرَهُ (daḥarahu), meaning he drove him off and removed him far away. It is a maf'ūl lahu (object of purpose). ﴿And for them﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿is a punishment, perpetual﴾, meaning lasting.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 37, verse 10:

﴿Except one who snatches away a snatching﴾ — "al-khatfah" is a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning a single instance; and the exception is from the pronoun in "yasammaʿūn" (they listen), i.e., none hears except the devil who heard the word from the angels and snatched it swiftly. ﴿So there follows him a flaming meteor﴾ — a shining star. ﴿Piercing﴾ — which pierces him, or burns him, or deprives him of his reason.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 37, verse 11:

﴿So ask them (fa-istaftihim)﴾ — seek information from the disbelievers of Makkah, either to establish (taqrir) or to rebuke (tawbikh): ﴿Are they stronger in creation, or those whom We have created?﴾ — of the angels, the heavens, the earths and what is between them. The use of "man" (min) here is to give precedence to rational beings (al-'uqala'). ﴿Indeed We created them﴾ — i.e., their origin, Adam — ﴿from clay (tin) that is sticky (lazib)﴾ — lazim, that clings to the hand. The meaning is that their creation is weak, so let them not be arrogant by denying the Prophet and the Qur'an, which would lead to their easy destruction.

(Bal) is for transition from one topic to another, namely the report about his state and theirs. ﴿Rather, you wonder﴾ with a fatha on the ta', addressed to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e., at their denying you. ﴿And they mock﴾ at your wondering.
﴿And when they are reminded﴾ [they are] admonished by the Qur'an, ﴿they do not remember﴾ [they do not] take heed.

And when they see a sign ﴿وإذا رَأَوْا آيَة﴾ — like the splitting of the moon — ﴿يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ﴾ they mock at it.

Note: the tafsir text reads: "﴿وإذا رَأَوْا آيَة﴾ كانْشِقاقِ القَمَر ﴿يَسْتَسْخِرُونَ﴾ يُسْتَهْزَءُونَ بِها"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 37, verse 15:

﴿And they say﴾ therein, ﴿"This is nothing but evident magic"﴾ clear. They say this, denying the Resurrection:

﴿Is it when we die and become dust and bones that we will indeed be raised up?﴾ Concerning the two hamzas (glottal stops) in the two places: tahqiq (full articulation) and tashil (easing) of the second, and inserting an alif between them, in both ways.

﴿Or our forefathers, the earliest ones﴾, read with a sukun on the waw (أوْ), as a conjunction ('atf) with أوْ (or), and with a fatha on it (أوَ) [meaning "and"]. The hamza (أ) is for interrogation (istifham). The conjunction with the waw (وَ) and the element conjoined (al-ma'tuf 'alayhi) occupy the grammatical position (mahall) of inna and its noun, or of the pronoun in ﴿لَمَبْعُوثُونَ﴾ [we shall indeed be raised], and the separator is the interrogative hamza.
